title: AfCFTA After Five Years: 50 Ratifications, 26 Tariff Schedules, $214bn of Trade | The Six, Ep. 8
lede: Trading under the African Continental Free Trade Area began on Jan. 1, 2021. Fifty countries have ratified and the rules of origin are now fully agreed, but only 26 have gazetted their tariff schedules. This episode looks at what has changed for traders, and what has not.
keyPoints: 54 of 55 AU members have signed the AfCFTA and 50 have ratified, Somalia most recently on Sept. 4, 2026; Benin, Libya, South Sudan and Sudan have not ratified (tralac, Sept. 2026).
By end-June 2026, 50 tariff schedules had been submitted, 48 verified and 26 gazetted. Rules of origin were 100% agreed after autos, clothing and textiles were adopted in February 2026.
More than 12,000 AfCFTA certificates of origin had been issued and notified to the Secretariat by March 2026 (AfCFTA Secretariat). Namibia had issued nine, its trade minister said in May 2026.
Intra-African trade was about $213.8 billion in 2025, up 5.5%, against about $1.5 trillion of total African merchandise trade (Afreximbank, African Trade Report 2026).
PAPSS now covers 28 countries, with 18 central banks and more than 190 commercial banks and fintechs; CEMAC banks are due to connect by the end of 2026 (Ecofin, July 2026).
